negativeResult.collection: John Gurney Senr estate inventory, Braintree, 16 March 1663 (SPR Case #338)
limitations: The inventory is a single appraisal snapshot at death; trade tools sold with the 1661/2 Monatiquot house, passed to a son, or worn out before March 1663 would leave no trace here.
The manuscript readings are a working transcription; a few low-value line items are abbreviated, but no plausible reading of any line yields a tailoring tool or a stock of cloth.
Appraisers routinely grouped small low-value goods; a needle-and-thread kit below their notice cannot be excluded, though shears, a pressing iron, or cloth stock would normally have been itemized.

sources.locator: Suffolk County Probate Records, Case #338, full inventory line-scan, 16 March 1663

statement: The 1663 estate inventory contains no tool or stock of the tailoring trade — no shears, needles, thimble, pressing- or goose-iron, yard-measure, or cloth/fabric — despite John being styled 'John Gurney, tailor' in his 1661/2 Monatiquot conveyance. The absence does not unsay the trade (the deed is direct evidence) but qualifies its centrality to his late-life economy, whose appraised value sat in land-rights and livestock; the 'pincers' listed beside the pewter are a general household/smith's tool, not a tailor's implement.
